derivation_justification: Sum of the three printed paid-work categories in one mutually exclusive, exhaustive employment-status variable: full-time 577 + part-time 284 + self-employed 68 = 929. The denominator is the printed cohort n minus the printed missing-data count, 16,862 - 551 = 16311, which is a subtraction of two printed counts and not a back-calculation from a percentage. The six categories sum to exactly 16,862 (577 + 284 + 12721 + 2661 + 68 + 551), and the three non-paid categories reconcile with the derived total: 929 employed + 12721 unemployed + 2661 retired = 16311 observed.
conflict_note: UNRESOLVED: one of the three components carries a published self-contradiction. Table 3 prints '577 (5.4)' for full-time employment in the relapse cohort while 577 of 16,862 is 3.4 per cent, and the relapse column's percentages sum to 102.0. The count 577 is corroborated by the column summing to exactly 16,862 and by the other five percentages checking out, and the same table's Table 1 sibling prints '587,581 (3.4)' for cancer in a cohort of 16,862, so the typesetting of this article is demonstrably unreliable. Under D12.3d only an author reply resolves a self-contradiction, so this derived total is blocked from every synthesis pending one.
notes: ZERO SEPARABILITY (D12.3): satisfied. These are mutually exclusive employment-STATUS categories, not intensity bands: every category containing positive paid work (full-time, part-time, self-employed) is separate from every category containing no paid work (unemployed, retired), so there is no residual band pooling zero work with low-intensity work. Contrast rautio2016, where the '<25.0%' band made paid_any unidentifiable. SELF-EMPLOYMENT is counted as paid work; the sibling cohort's own review literature and nossel2018's definition both treat self-employment as paid employment. It is not counted as competitive because this report establishes no labour-market setting. DENOMINATOR: n_outcome_observed = 16311, the printed 16,862 minus the printed 551/501 with missing employment data. reported_percentage_base = 16,862 because the authors' own percentages divide by the full matched cohort including the missing category (12,721/16,862 = 75.4 exactly, as printed). NO HORIZON: followup_basis = unclear and followup_months is left blank. The outcome is 'based on the most recent nonmissing data during the study period', the study period runs 1 January 2013 to 30 September 2019 and includes the 12-month pre-index baseline, and the authors state that 'because a cross-sectional approach was used in examining societal outcomes across the full study period, no temporality was applied between the exposure (relapse) and the outcomes of interest'. Mean follow-up was 4.7 years but that is the length of the observation window, not the time at which employment was measured, so no elapsed time from cohort entry can be assigned and no landmark horizon applies. ARM: this is a propensity-score-matched relapse subgroup of the 119,343-veteran schizophrenia cohort, not a whole recruited cohort, so it cannot enter the primary prevalence estimand (SAP 2.1 and 7) irrespective of the conflict status. MODERATOR: only the male count is printed (15,499 of 16,862); the sex variable is not shown to be exhaustive, so n_female is left blank rather than derived by complement.

derivation_justification: Sum of the three printed paid-work categories in one mutually exclusive, exhaustive employment-status variable: full-time 908 + part-time 428 + self-employed 93 = 1429. The denominator is the printed cohort n minus the printed missing-data count, 16,862 - 501 = 16361, which is a subtraction of two printed counts and not a back-calculation from a percentage. The six categories sum to exactly 16,862 (908 + 428 + 12043 + 2889 + 93 + 501), and the three non-paid categories reconcile with the derived total: 1429 employed + 12043 unemployed + 2889 retired = 16361 observed.
notes: ZERO SEPARABILITY (D12.3): satisfied. These are mutually exclusive employment-STATUS categories, not intensity bands: every category containing positive paid work (full-time, part-time, self-employed) is separate from every category containing no paid work (unemployed, retired), so there is no residual band pooling zero work with low-intensity work. Contrast rautio2016, where the '<25.0%' band made paid_any unidentifiable. SELF-EMPLOYMENT is counted as paid work; the sibling cohort's own review literature and nossel2018's definition both treat self-employment as paid employment. It is not counted as competitive because this report establishes no labour-market setting. DENOMINATOR: n_outcome_observed = 16361, the printed 16,862 minus the printed 551/501 with missing employment data. reported_percentage_base = 16,862 because the authors' own percentages divide by the full matched cohort including the missing category (12,721/16,862 = 75.4 exactly, as printed). NO HORIZON: followup_basis = unclear and followup_months is left blank. The outcome is 'based on the most recent nonmissing data during the study period', the study period runs 1 January 2013 to 30 September 2019 and includes the 12-month pre-index baseline, and the authors state that 'because a cross-sectional approach was used in examining societal outcomes across the full study period, no temporality was applied between the exposure (relapse) and the outcomes of interest'. Mean follow-up was 4.9 years but that is the length of the observation window, not the time at which employment was measured, so no elapsed time from cohort entry can be assigned and no landmark horizon applies. ARM: this is a propensity-score-matched nonrelapse subgroup of the 119,343-veteran schizophrenia cohort, not a whole recruited cohort, so it cannot enter the primary prevalence estimand (SAP 2.1 and 7) irrespective of the conflict status. MODERATOR: only the male count is printed (15,529 of 16,862); the sex variable is not shown to be exhaustive, so n_female is left blank rather than derived by complement.
